**Status: detailed implementation plan; comparison targets are not wired.**
[`data_checks.R`][legacy-checks] contains several investigations, reused
variable names, and experimental comparisons. This page organizes those
questions into reproducible evidence. It does not turn every scratch
expression into an accepted scientific assertion.

The [mapping notebook](mapping/legacy-pipeline-map.qmd#script-checks-exploratory-checks-and-supplements)
retains the assignment-level inventory. Source inspection stays on page 17;
each transformation owns its own rule tests; this page owns the comparisons
between the legacy and replacement products.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Agree On The Comparison Contract"}

Identify the exact input freeze, source-code revision, prepared Wave 3 schema,
dictionary revision, and legacy reference artifacts. Track references as
source file targets or members of the already tracked archive. A file with
the right name is not sufficient evidence of matching provenance.

For every comparison, record its row grain, alignment keys, duplicate policy,
column correspondence, missing/sentinel semantics, and any numeric or spatial
tolerance. Review intentional differences before calling the migration
equivalent. Newer exports such as 2023 deliveries are separate datasets until
their source contract is established.

Keep the raw input tree immutable. No validation procedure overwrites the
reference or promotes a derived supplement into the raw source inventory.
Protected discrepancy rows remain in governed targets/artifacts and are not
rendered into the public manual.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Classify The Legacy Investigations Before Porting Them"}

| Legacy responsibility | Planned owner and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Export/file/schema inventories | Page 17 and `schecks_source_export_tables_list`; record periods, columns, and source provenance |
| Reader experiments | Page 18's reader tests plus `schecks_csv_reader_comparison_list`; explain encoding, sparse typing, quotes, and name repair |
| Wave 3 preparation comparisons | This page; keyed equality and discrepancy summaries against a fixed prepared reference |
| Dictionary comparisons | This page; expressions, ordered schemas, translations, and harmonized IDs evaluated separately |
| Mumps year/subset exports | Explicit optional diagnostic projections in procedures, stored as targets/Parquet outside the raw tree |
| Transformation-specific assertions | The check block of the page that owns the transformation |

The repeated late-2023 comparison that reads a 2022 object needs a corrected,
explicit source selection before it can support a conclusion. The exploratory
numeric matrix that compares the old object with itself cannot establish
old/new agreement. Do not carry those mistakes into a regression test.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Build Small Alignment And Schema Contracts"}

Use `schecks_w3_legacy_comparison_inputs_list` and
`schecks_dictionary_legacy_comparison_inputs_list` as small reference/path
contracts rather than lists of fully loaded measurement tables. Record
ordered names, types, row grain, key uniqueness, and source hashes or tracked
target identities in `schecks_migration_contract_list`.

Validate keys before sorting or joining: a many-to-many join can multiply
rows and disguise a mismatch. When legitimate repeated keys exist, define
their comparison unit explicitly rather than assigning a new row number
whose order differs between storage engines. Check equality of key sets and
multiplicity before comparing values.

Use page 21's recorded `X` schema to compare dictionary references. Ignore a
legacy export index only when it is proven to be an IO artifact, not a
scientific identifier. Never renumber `V` or `X` variables merely to make the
tables look equal.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Compare Large Measurement Products In DuckDB"}

Read tracked Parquet paths as relations. Project a limited variable set or
period partition, align on the agreed keys, and compute counts of missing
keys and unequal values. Collect only small summaries for the manager.
Persist governed discrepancy records as `schecks_w3_value_mismatches_parquet`
when row-level evidence is needed.

The plan replaces full in-memory comparison matrices with keyed comparison
relations. Test the comparator itself using unequal fixtures: new-only and
old-only rows, duplicate keys, permuted row order, changed numeric values,
and differing missing values must produce failures or explicit discrepancy
records. A passing self-comparison is only a sanity check.

Compare entered zero, missing, `-1`, and `-99` separately according to the
owning transformation's contract. Do not convert all missing values to
infinity or all logical columns to numeric as an unexplained equality fix.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Compare Dictionary Semantics Before Output Labels"}

Build `schecks_dictionary_migration_report_df` from the new dictionary, its
recorded source schemas, and the chosen legacy reference. Compare the wave
expressions, repeated summands, unavailable-wave semantics, output groups,
French descriptions, and English translation provenance separately.

If `V` numbering differs, first compare the ordered inputs and expression
identity. Produce an explicit old/new expression crosswalk for review rather
than rewriting either dictionary. An apparent translation-only difference
must not conceal a changed clinical definition or age band.

Reuse page 21's synthetic validator and archive-translation coverage checks.
Do not invoke a live translation service during validation to refresh the
reference or fill a comparison gap.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Keep Mumps Diagnostic Projections Outside The Raw Tree"}

Inventory the combined 2021–2022 mumps export in
`schecks_mumps_source_df` only if small enough for the stated memory budget;
otherwise use a source file target and DuckDB relation. Separate year views in
`schecks_mumps_by_year_list` and the named 2021 male 2–11-month projection in
`schecks_mumps_2021_males_2_11m_df`, or persist their larger equivalents as
`schecks_mumps_output_parquet`.

Preserve the exact source header `T4: Oreillon 2-11m, Masculin`, period filter,
and metadata-column selection. Check year coverage and the relationship of
the subset to its parent without writing `oreillon_2021.csv` or other derived
files back into `data/inputs`.

These are diagnostic projections unless explicitly adopted as a curation
input. If a repair becomes authoritative, implement it in the owning source
preparation procedure and add a visible dependency to pages 18 or 22. It must
not enter the analysis through an undocumented raw-directory side effect.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Assemble A Migration Evidence Report"}

`schecks_migration_report_list` will combine small reports from identities,
dictionary construction, diagnoses, spatial assignments, locations, and the
two metadata products. Larger row-level evidence remains in tracked Parquet;
geometry comparisons remain in ordinary spatial targets.

| Report field | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| Provenance | Input/reference revisions, code revision, environment and geometry-engine versions |
| Alignment | Grain, keys, key counts/multiplicity, and column/schema correspondence |
| Results | Exact matches, measured discrepancies, missing coverage, and resource observations |
| Decisions | Accepted differences, rationale, accountable review, and unresolved items |
| Artifacts | Target names and tracked evidence paths; no ambiguous scratch filenames |

Keep validation separate from release approval. This evidence informs the
[release contract](../releases/19_page-package-release.qmd); it does not
authorize publishing protected data or decide a scientific discrepancy on
the reviewer's behalf.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Specify Evidence And Comparator Acceptance"}

Create `tests/check-migration-comparators.R` before wiring comparison targets.
The tests must show that each comparator detects an injected mismatch, handles
missing values and legitimate multiplicity according to its contract, and
does not report equality when its two inputs differ.

After a separately authorized build, the final checks should confirm:

- every required comparison has identifiable inputs and a completed result;
- key coverage, schema references, and expression/sentinel tests satisfy the
  approved contract;
- each remaining discrepancy is either an accepted, documented change or an
  unresolved failure that prevents an equivalence claim;
- parallel and serial execution produce the same canonically compared data;
- a second build with unchanged inputs rebuilds no scientific targets;
- evidence artifacts exist, remain under governed destinations, and can be
  inspected without loading all measurements into R.

Historical numerical comments in `data_checks.R` are comparison hypotheses,
not newly observed outcomes. No comparison or scientific pipeline has been
executed while writing this plan.

```sh
python3 tests/check-manual-structure.py
```
